answer: Proof-of-stake Sybil defense makes identity expensive: every agent must lock collateral to serve as a bridge between payment channels. The ledger keeps a public mirror of each bond so one sable token cannot be counted twice, and each new alias must post its own fresh stake. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand independent bonds, so the capital cost grows linearly with the number of identities rather than with raw compute.
